Mildly positive on growth but deliberately cautious on inflation and policy stance. In the Clarida, Galí, and Gertler monetary-policy framework, keeping the funds rate at 4.25–4.50% while noting “inflation remains somewhat elevated” is consistent with a Taylor-type, inflation‑responsive rule that restrains the otherwise upbeat signals on activity and employment. The emphasis on monitoring inflation expectations and being “prepared to adjust” matches Svensson and Woodford’s risk‑management approach to policymaking under uncertainty, while continued balance‑sheet runoff and standing facility settings reinforce a restrictive posture. Inflation‑at‑risk work likewise supports guarding against right‑tail inflation outcomes despite solid growth, and the nod to swings in net exports recognizes real‑time output-gap measurement issues highlighted in the literature. Netting these elements, the communication reads neutral‑to‑slightly positive rather than distinctly upbeat.

“economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.”
